title: Mother's Secret
next_chapter_hook: The last scene of the memory fragment—Chen Ji saw the words his mother spoke to him as an infant in swaddling clothes before her death: 'My child, your fate you shall write yourself.' Yet this time, he clearly saw in those gentle eyes a trace of guilt he had never understood before.

text.content: Chen Ji stood frozen. The jade pendant lay quietly in Su Qingyao's palm, its warm touch conveying through his fingertips a familiar scent that was almost suffocating—it was his mother's scent. On the back of the jade pendant, a name was clearly visible: Chen Nian. That was the name of his sister, separated from him since infancy, and also the clue he had been investigating for years. Yet why would this jade pendant, which should have disappeared with his sister, bear his sister's name and appear in Su Qingyao's hands? 'Where did you get this?' His voice was hoarse, unlike his own.

dialogue.content: 'At your mother's grave.' Su Qingyao did not hide the truth. 'This jade pendant was a testament letter she entrusted someone to deliver before her death, instructing me to give it to you when you were ready.' She paused, her gaze complicated: 'She also said something else—"This child carries too heavy a burden. Unless absolutely necessary, do not let him know."'

text.content: Chen Ji took the jade pendant, his fingertips brushing over the familiar name. Memories surged like a tide—the expression on his mother's face at death's door, the force with which her withered fingers gripped his clothes, and those words he had always thought were meaningless babble spoken to an infant. Only now did he understand they were not babble. The pendant's surface suddenly glowed faintly, and a remnant consciousness钻入 his brow center along his touch. In an instant, the world spun, and Chen Ji was pulled into a hazy light and shadow.

The light and shadow swayed like reflections in water, gradually forming a woman's silhouette. It was a gentle and beautiful face, with seven-tenths resemblance to Chen Ji. She wore plain white robes, seated in a quiet mountain cave, surrounded by faint golden patterns—those were the unique Tianji marks of a prophet. In the scene, she was gazing down at the jade pendant in her hands, tears still wet on her cheeks.

dialogue.content: (Memory) The woman murmured softly, her voice gentle yet resolute: 'Jiang Xueyao, forty-eighth generation candidate for Prophet... this was my name once. The Tianji Record chose me to become the next vessel. But it did not tell me that those who become prophets will completely lose themselves, becoming puppets of Heavenly Will.'

text.content: Chen Ji's heart shuddered. Jiang Xueyao—this was his mother's maiden name he had never known. He only knew her as Chen Jiangshi, an ordinary woman from a distant branch of the Chen family, with delicate features but no cultivation. So from the beginning, this was all a deception. The scene shifted, and the woman raised her head, her gaze seeming to pierce through time to meet Chen Ji's eyes: 'My child, when you see this memory, it means you have found the Tianji Record Fragment.'

dialogue.content: 'Every prophet chosen by the Tianji Record was not accidentally selected, but meticulously cultivated as a bloodline chess piece. The bloodlines of successive prophets are recorded, screened, and matched, all to nurture the most perfect vessel.' Her voice trembled slightly: 'The Chen family is precisely one of the breeding families for successive prophets.'

text.content: Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply. The Chen family—that ordinary remote branch he had thought, those few brief records he had seen in the family genealogy. So his bloodline was never accidental from the start. The memory continued flowing. Jiang Xueyao stood before an ancient altar, her bloodline guided by golden threads, converging into a fragmented jade slip at the altar's center.

dialogue.content: 'I was the closest to success among the forty-eighth generation candidates.' Jiang Xueyao laughed bitterly. 'They spent thirty years cultivating me into the perfect vessel, never knowing I discovered a secret in secret—' She raised her hand, and a faint spiritual light appeared in her palm: 'The Tianji Record's shackles have a gap. Any combination of non-family bloodlines with Chen family bloodline may give birth to a "variable."'

text.content: Variable. This word struck Chen Ji's heart like a heavy hammer. The scene switched. Jiang Xueyao had left the altar, walking alone on a desolate mountain path. Behind her, the outline of Tianqing Sect loomed faintly through the clouds—that was precisely where Chen Ji was born. 'So you married into the Chen family.' Chen Ji murmured to himself, his voice bitter. 'To rebel against their arrangement.'

dialogue.content: (Memory) Jiang Xueyao's figure appeared before a simple farmhouse, her belly slightly rounded. She gently stroked her abdomen, eyes filled with both tenderness and guilt. 'Chen De, a remote Chen family member.' she said softly. 'A man with no cultivation, ignorant of the inside story. I chose him because his bloodline was dilute enough not to alert those people.' 'And the child in my womb will be the key to breaking the shackles—the only variable.'

text.content: Chen Ji's fingernails dug deeply into his palms, blood seeping out without him noticing. His father—that silent man in his memories, who had died of illness long ago—was actually a tool from the very beginning. A tool to conceal the truth and protect his growth. And his mother—that plain, simple woman in his eyes—had once been a rebel standing at the edge of fate's chessboard. The memory flowed on, depicting the rainy night of his birth.

In the rainy night, Jiang Xueyao lay on a simple bed, sweat and blood mixing together. The midwife's panicked voice rang out repeatedly, but her eyes held only calm. An infant's cry broke the silence. She took the child, and a relieved smile bloomed on her pale face: 'It's a boy.' After the midwife left, she placed the child in a wooden basin, letting the rain fall on her face, murmuring: 'From now on, you are no longer the bloodline of a prophet, just the son of a废物.'

dialogue.content: '废物, is that right?' Jiang Xueyao in the memory laughed lowly, tears glistening in her eyes. 'Let them think you are废物. That way, they won't discover the truth before you finish growing.' 'You are the most perfect variable I could think of—the combination of Chen family bloodline and a non-family name, judged by the Tianji Record as a "failed product," yet precisely thereby avoiding all surveillance.' She lightly kissed the infant's forehead: 'Your fate, from the moment of your birth, no longer belongs to them.'

text.content: Chen Ji felt his eyes growing hot. He had thought he was a废物 who had stumbled upon the Tianji Record by chance, not knowing that everything about him—including the废物 persona—was a protective color his mother had woven for him with her life. The scene shifted, the timeline jumping to when he was five years old. Jiang Xueyao's appearance had grown much haggard. She knelt alone before a solitary grave, in which stood a blank stone tablet.

dialogue.content: (Memory) 'Chen De, I'm sorry.' Jiang Xueyao murmured to the gravestone. 'You should never have been drawn into all this, yet you died because of me.' She stood up, turning to look at the child's back playing in the grass hut in the distance: 'But I do not regret. Your death traded for Ji'er's safety—they thought the variable had gone with you.' 'Next, I will take him away from here and sever all clues.'

text.content: The memory cut off abruptly. Chen Ji jerked back to reality, finding himself still gripping the jade pendant, his body soaked in cold sweat. Su Qingyao stood not far away, gazing at him with complex eyes. 'What did you see?' she asked softly. Chen Ji did not answer. His mind was still echoing with his mother's final words—that truth about variables, about shackles, about his entire life being a meticulously designed scheme.

choice.prompt: Mother wove the chess game of fate for him with her entire life, and now the truth is revealed. Does he accept this heavy gift from bloodline, or personally shatter this seemingly perfect arrangement?

choices.description: Mother's protection bought with her life cannot be wasted. Continue walking as a废物, secretly accumulating strength.
choices.visible_reward: Stabilize the existing layout, reduce exposure risk
choices.risk_hint: If the truth becomes known to others, the废物 persona will completely collapse

text.content:
Chen Ji took a deep breath and tucked the Jade Pendant into his chest.

"I understand." His voice regained its calm, as if everything just moments ago was merely an illusion. "Thank you for telling me all this, Sister Su Qingyao."

He raised his head, his gaze deep as an abyss: "But there's one thing you need to understand—from now on, you have been drawn into a chess game far beyond your imagination."

choices.description: He refused to be a piece on someone else's chessboard anymore, even if the chess player was his own mother.
choices.visible_reward: Potential possibility to break the shackles, awaken the true power of the Variable
choices.risk_hint: May trigger the backlash mechanism of the Tianji Record

text.content:
Chen Ji forcefully crushed the teacup in his palm, the broken porcelain piercing his skin as blood dripped down.

"Enough." His voice was terrifyingly cold. "I won't deny the value of the protection my mother spent her life weaving for me. But—"

He raised his head, flames burning in his eyes: "I, Chen Ji, from this day forward, will no longer be anyone's piece. The shackles of the Tianji Record, I will break with my own hands."

choices.description: Mother's words may not all be true, perhaps there are deeper secrets waiting to be uncovered.
choices.visible_reward: Obtain more crucial information, avoid impulsive decisions
choices.risk_hint: The truth may be even more cruel

text.content:
Chen Ji closed his eyes, forcing himself to calm down.

"I believe my mother's words. But—" He opened his eyes, his gaze sharp as a blade. "Her memories are from ten years ago. What has happened in those ten years, she may not know."

He turned to Su Qingyao: "Sister Su Qingyao, what else do you know about this Jade Pendant?"

No matter what choice he made, the memories within the Jade Pendant continued to flow.

The final image emerged—it was the scene of Jiang Xueyao on her deathbed. She lay on the worn cot, her face withered, yet she remained lucid.

Chen De was dead, Chen Nian was missing, only the young Chen Ji sat by the bedside, gazing blankly at his departing mother.

Her trembling hand caressed Chen Ji's cheek, tears rolling down, yet she smiled as she spoke those words—

dialogue.content:
(Memory) "My child, your destiny shall be written by yourself."

With her last strength, she left a kiss on Chen Ji's brow center. A wisp of faint light emerged from her brow center and entered Chen Ji's brow center—that was the remnants of her Heavenly Secrets power as an aspiring Prophet.

"Go... leave here... find your sister... she is... is..."

The voice cut off abruptly. Jiang Xueyao's hand fell, her eyes closing forever.

text.content:
The memories completely dissipated.

Chen Ji stood there, trembling all over. He finally understood his mother's last unfinished words—Chen Nian was the "Heavenly Fate Key," an existence even more special than the Variable.

But why did his mother's memories only fully manifest at this moment?

His gaze fell upon the Jade Pendant, and he suddenly noticed that besides the characters "Chen Nian" on the back, there was an extremely small line of text, nearly worn away by time.

He leaned in close to examine it, his pupils constricting sharply—it was a set of coordinates, pointing to a certain forbidden area in the Tianqing Sect Back Mountain.

Tianqing Sect Back Mountain Forbidden Grounds.

That was the area where he was assigned to sweep as a Servant Disciple after being judged as waste by the Sect's elders. It was also where he discovered the first page fragment of the Tianji Record.

Coincidence?

Chen Ji sneered coldly. He tucked the Jade Pendant into his chest, turned, and gazed at the gradually darkening sky outside the window.

The chess game his mother had laid out with her life, he accepted. But from now on, he would personally grasp the chess pieces, rather than being a piece pushed along the board.

"Chen Nian..." he murmured his sister's name, "Wait for me."
